THE INCIDENT THIS FIXES, real, this week. A guest emailed his headshot ("prof headshot minimized.webp") and his links (his website, his own podcast) weeks before publication. server/pipeline/guest_assets.py existed, fully tested, and returned all of it on the first call. NOTHING CALLED IT. The episode published with a thumbnail that did not use the guest's face and show notes carrying only a CRM-scraped LinkedIn URL. The owner caught it by eye after publication.

WHERE TO WIRE, precisely. In server/pipeline/orchestrator.py, the qa-passed block (~line 4470) generates all artwork:
    title = content.get("title", ep.topic or "Episode")
    guest_photo, guest_name, guest_title = _guest_artwork_fields(ep)
    artwork = generate_episode_artwork(...)
and _guest_artwork_fields (~line 4466) currently reads only guest.get("brand_headshot_path") / photo_url / linkedin photo_url — CRM-derived fields. The guest's EMAIL is never consulted.

THE FIX:
1. Add a method/helper around the qa-passed artwork block: BEFORE computing
   _guest_artwork_fields, run guest-assets collection when the first guest has an email:
     from server.pipeline import guest_assets as ga
     from server.pipeline.emails import EmailClient
   Build the client via EmailClient() (its _get_service() is the exact seam
   guest_email_context._gmail_service accepts; it fails closed without credentials).
   Call ga.collect_guest_assets(client, guest_email, dest_dir=<episode raw dir>/
   "guest-assets", existing_links=<the guest's current links dict if any>).
   The construction of the client and the collection call must be wrapped so ANY failure
   (no credentials, network) degrades: record and continue — publication is never blocked
   by a missing headshot. Make the client injectable for tests (module-level factory or
   parameter), matching how the rest of orchestrator handles seams.
2. Persist the result on the episode: ep._data["guest_assets"] = {"headshot_path",
   "links", "skipped", "report": ga.assets_report(result)} and merge the returned links
   into the first guest's record (guest-email links WIN over CRM values for the same key,
   keys only in CRM are preserved — collect_guest_assets already merges; store its output).
3. Make _guest_artwork_fields prefer the collected emailed headshot: highest priority
   becomes ep._data["guest_assets"]["headshot_path"] when set, then the existing chain
   (brand_headshot_path, photo_url, linkedin photo_url) unchanged.
4. When collection was attempted and found nothing, ep._data["guest_assets"] must still
   exist with the report naming the absence ("no headshot found in guest email") — the
   silent version of this failure is what shipped the bad thumbnail.
5. Do not change: artwork QA, publish flow, any email sending, any other stage.

TESTS (tests/test_guest_assets_orchestrator.py; at least 6, fake client, tmp episode dirs;
read tests/test_guest_assets_wiring.py for the established fake-client pattern):
 (1) THE REAL CASE: guest with email + fake client carrying an image/webp attachment →
     after the qa-passed artwork step (call the smallest orchestrator unit that runs the
     wiring, or the helper directly plus an assertion it is invoked from the artwork
     path), ep._data["guest_assets"]["headshot_path"] is set and _guest_artwork_fields
     returns it FIRST;
 (2) NEGATIVE: client construction raises (no credentials) → episode proceeds, and
     ep._data["guest_assets"] records the degradation with a reason — never an exception,
     never silence;
 (3) guest-email links merged into the guest record with guest-email winning on
     conflicts and CRM-only keys preserved;
 (4) NEGATIVE: guest with NO email → no client construction attempted (assert factory
     not called), and ep._data["guest_assets"] records why collection was skipped;
 (5) NEGATIVE: collection returns no headshot → _guest_artwork_fields falls back to the
     existing chain AND the persisted report names the absence;
 (6) the wiring runs before generate_episode_artwork in the qa-passed path (assert
     ordering via the fakes — the artwork call must see the emailed headshot path).
Keep tests/test_guest_assets_wiring.py green.

OWNED FILES (only these — both new):
  scripts/export_dag_projection.py
  tests/test_dag_projection_export.py

WHY. The owner's governance layer (a separate supervisory department) must be able to see, for every episode, which DAG steps ran, which were skipped WITH a valid skip artifact, and which were skipped silently. The pipeline stays the single execution authority; this script is the pipeline's outward-facing receipt: a versioned, content-hashed projection the supervisor consumes read-only. The supervisor is being built against this exact contract in parallel, so the shape is FROZEN.

THE FROZEN PROJECTION CONTRACT (dag-projection-v1) — both sides of the system build
against this exact shape; do not extend or rename fields:
{
  "schema": "dag-projection-v1",
  "generated_at": "<iso8601 UTC>",
  "source_ref": "<git sha of the podcast repo the projection was built from>",
  "dag_hash": "<sha256 hex of the canonical JSON (sort_keys, compact separators) of the
               steps list below — recomputable by any consumer>",
  "steps": [{"id": str, "requires": [str], "produces": [str], "optional": bool}],
  "episodes": [{
      "episode_id": str, "stage": str,
      "completed": [str],
      "skip_artifacts": {"<step_id>": <episode-skip-v1 artifact dict>},
      "audit": {"complete": bool, "silent_skips": [str],
                "authorized_skips": [str], "invalid_skips": [str]}
  }]
}

BUILD scripts/export_dag_projection.py:
  * Imports server.pipeline.episode_dag (EPISODE_DAG, audit_run, validate_skip_artifact —
    read that module first; it defines episode-skip-v1 artifacts and audit_run semantics).
  * build_projection(episodes_dir, *, now, source_ref) -> dict in the frozen shape.
    Per episode directory containing episode.json: derive "completed" from the episode's
    recorded state as honestly as possible — read episode.json and map what the pipeline
    actually records (stage, timestamps like warmup_sent_at, artifacts on disk such as
    final render/certification receipts) to DAG step ids via a single explicit
    STEP_EVIDENCE table in the script: {step_id: callable(ep_data, episode_dir) -> bool}.
    Every step id in EPISODE_DAG must have an entry; a step with no honest evidence
    source maps to False (never guess completion). Read skip artifacts from
    <episode_dir>/skips/<step_id>.json when present. Run audit_run with those inputs and
    embed its verdict per episode.
  * dag_hash: sha256 hex of the canonical JSON (sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")) of
    the steps list — the supervisor recomputes this to detect projection/DAG drift.
  * main(): --episodes-dir, --output (default stdout), --source-ref (default: `git
    rev-parse HEAD` of the repo; subprocess allowed here only). Exit 0 on success; exit 2
    when ANY episode has silent_skips or invalid_skips (the projection still prints —
    the nonzero exit is the tripwire for cron), exit 1 on structural failure.
  * Unreadable episode.json is NOT skipped silently: the episode appears with
    stage "unreadable" and audit.complete false. That failure mode (silently continuing
    past unreadable episodes) caused real missed sends in this repo's cron this month.

TESTS (tests/test_dag_projection_export.py; at least 6, tmp episode dirs):
 (1) an episode with evidence for a completed prefix of steps yields those steps in
     "completed" and dag_hash equals an independently recomputed sha256 in the test;
 (2) a valid skip artifact (created via episode_dag.make_skip_artifact) in
     skips/<step>.json lands in skip_artifacts and audit reports it authorized;
 (3) NEGATIVE: a tampered skip artifact appears in invalid_skips and main exits 2;
 (4) NEGATIVE: an unreadable episode.json produces stage "unreadable",
     audit.complete false — present, never dropped;
 (5) determinism: identical inputs (fixed `now`, fixed source_ref) → byte-identical
     projection JSON;
 (6) every step id in EPISODE_DAG has a STEP_EVIDENCE entry (assert the table's keys
     equal the DAG's step ids, so adding a DAG step without an evidence mapping fails
     the suite);
 (7) NEGATIVE: an episode with a downstream step completed but a required upstream step
     neither completed nor skip-authorized shows that step in silent_skips and exit is 2.
Keep tests/test_episode_dag.py and tests/test_skip_artifacts.py green (do not edit them).
